phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Ra.
phrases.explanation: These detached letters open the chapter, and early interpreters explained them in several ways. Some said each letter stands as an abbreviation for one of the names or attributes of God, or serves as an opening oath by which God swears to the truth of the revelation. Others said they are a title for the chapter or a challenge showing that the Quran is composed of the very letters the Arabs use in speech, while the ultimate meaning rests with God.

phrases.translation: These are the verses of the Book; the clear Quran
phrases.explanation: These revealed passages belong to the divine Scripture and form a clear, eloquent recitation that makes the truth unmistakable to anyone who hears and reflects upon it. Some early commentators explained that the Book refers to the preserved scripture with God, or to the earlier revealed scriptures, joined here with the clear Quran sent down to the Prophet. It distinguishes guidance from error and sets out God’s commands, promises, and warnings in plain Arabic.

phrases.translation: ˹The day will come when˺ the disbelievers will certainly wish they had submitted ˹to Allah˺
phrases.explanation: In Arabic usage from God, the word translated as perhaps expresses certainty that a day is coming when those who rejected faith will deeply wish they had surrendered to God in Islam. Commentators differed over when this regret takes place. Some said it occurs at the moment of death or on Judgment Day when they see the punishment, while others said it happens in Hell when sinful monotheists are finally brought out of the Fire through intercession and mercy.

phrases.translation: ˹So˺ let them eat and enjoy themselves and be diverted by ˹false˺ hope,
phrases.explanation: God instructs the Prophet to leave the stubborn polytheists to eat, take temporary pleasure in their worldly life, and remain distracted by vain hopes of long life and continued prosperity. This command is not a permission to sin, but a stern warning and threat of what awaits them. Their brief indulgence and false expectations only lull them into heedlessness while they neglect the truth and fail to prepare for the reckoning ahead.

phrases.translation: for they will soon know
phrases.explanation: They will soon discover the bitter outcome of their disbelief, mockery, and attachment to worldly desires when God’s punishment overtakes them in this life or when they stand before Him in the hereafter. At that moment all their false hopes will vanish, and they will know with certainty that what the Messenger warned them about was the undeniable truth from which they have no escape.

phrases.translation: We have never destroyed a society without a destined term
phrases.explanation: God has never annihilated any town or nation for its tyranny and disbelief except at a fixed, written time already decreed in His knowledge. Even when a people persist in rebellion, their respite runs until the exact moment appointed for them arrives. When that predetermined deadline is reached, neither can they delay the punishment by a single hour nor can it come before its decreed term.

phrases.translation: No people can advance their doom, nor can they delay it
phrases.explanation: No community can bring forward its appointed time of destruction before the deadline God has decreed, nor can it push that time back once it arrives. This reassures the Prophet and warns the Meccan disbelievers not to be deceived by the delay of their punishment. Their temporary safety does not mean God is unaware of them, but only that their fixed term has not yet expired.

phrases.translation: They say, “O you to whom the Reminder is revealed!
phrases.explanation: The leaders of Quraysh addressed the Prophet in a tone of open mockery and sarcasm, calling him the one upon whom the Reminder had supposedly been sent down. By the Reminder they meant the Quran, yet they used this title only in derision, not because they believed that God had truly revealed a scripture to him. They sought to belittle his prophetic claim in front of their followers.

phrases.translation: You must be insane
phrases.explanation: Because the Prophet called them to abandon their ancestral idols, affirm the oneness of God, and prepare for resurrection and judgment, the disbelievers accused him of madness. In their arrogance, they treated his willingness to part from the religion of his forefathers and to warn them of an unseen reckoning as proof that he had lost his mind or was possessed.

phrases.translation: Why do you not bring us the angels, if what you say is true?”
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers challenged the Prophet to bring angels down before their eyes to testify that he was truly God’s Messenger, or to bring the punishment he had warned them about, if he was telling the truth. Rather than examining the clear proofs of the Quran itself, they demanded a visible spectacle of angels as a stubborn excuse to persist in their denial.

phrases.translation: We do not send the angels down except for a just cause,
phrases.explanation: God replies that He does not send the angels down in visible form at the whim of mocking disbelievers, but only with truth and a decisive decree. Early interpreters explained that this just cause means the revealed message given to the prophets, or the final command of death and destruction when God decides to annihilate a stubborn nation that has rejected every warning.

phrases.translation: and then ˹the end of˺ the disbelievers will not be delayed
phrases.explanation: If the angels were sent down to them in person with God’s decree of punishment, as they recklessly demanded, the disbelievers would not be granted a single moment of delay. Just as happened to earlier nations when the angels of torment arrived, their chance for repentance would immediately end and they would be destroyed on the spot without reprieve.

phrases.translation: It is certainly We Who have revealed the Reminder, and it is certainly We Who will preserve it
phrases.explanation: God emphatically affirms that He Himself sent down the Quran in response to the disbelievers’ mockery, and that He alone guarantees its complete protection. It is preserved from any addition, deletion, distortion, or falsehood so that no opponent can alter its words or extinguish its message. Some commentators also noted that God protects the Prophet himself from his enemies so the revelation is safely delivered.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We sent messengers before you ˹O Prophet˺ among the groups of early peoples
phrases.explanation: God consoles the Prophet by reminding him that many messengers were sent before him to the communities, classes, and factions of earlier nations who lived long before Quraysh. Despite their different eras and lands, those ancient peoples reacted to God’s messengers with the very same arrogance and hostility that the Meccan polytheists now show toward the Prophet.

phrases.translation: but no messenger ever came to them without being mocked
phrases.explanation: Whenever a messenger came to any of those ancient nations with clear guidance from God, the disbelievers among them ridiculed him and treated his warnings as a joke. By recalling this consistent history, God comforts the Prophet and urges him to bear his people’s insults with patience, knowing that every true messenger before him endured the same mockery before God’s promise was fulfilled.

phrases.translation: This is how We allow disbelief ˹to steep˺ into the hearts of the wicked
phrases.explanation: Just as disbelief, mockery, and stubborn denial took root in the hearts of those ancient nations who ridiculed their messengers, the same attitude enters the hearts of the wicked polytheists among the Prophet’s own people. Because they choose obstinacy over reflection, denial penetrates their hearts until they remain trapped in the same blindness that brought ruin upon earlier communities.

phrases.translation: They would not believe in this ˹Quran˺ despite the ˹many˺ examples of those ˹destroyed˺ before
phrases.explanation: Those whose hearts are steeped in wickedness will not believe in the Quran or accept the Prophet’s call, even though the well-known way of God with earlier nations has already passed before them. The ruins and stories of how God destroyed ancient peoples who mocked their prophets are clear lessons, yet the Meccan disbelievers ignore those warnings and repeat the same fatal mistake.

phrases.translation: And even if We opened for them a gate to heaven, through which they continued to ascend
phrases.explanation: God describes the extreme stubbornness of the Meccan disbelievers who demanded visible miracles and angels. Even if God were to open a literal doorway in the sky and allow them to climb through it in broad daylight, ascending higher and higher while beholding the wonders of the heavens and the angels with their own eyes, their hardened hearts would still refuse to submit.

phrases.translation: still they would say, “Our eyes have truly been dazzled! In fact, we must have been bewitched.”
phrases.explanation: Rather than believing after witnessing such an unmistakable miracle, they would immediately invent an excuse to deny what they saw. They would claim that their sight had been blocked, tricked, or confused, and that Muhammad had cast a powerful spell over them to make them imagine ascending into the sky. When a heart is determined to reject the truth, no physical sign can compel it to believe.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We have placed constellations in the sky, and adorned it for all to see
phrases.explanation: Turning from their stubborn demands to the real signs already filling the universe, God reminds humanity that He placed great mansions and constellations in the sky for the sun, moon, and stars. Through these celestial stations time, seasons, and directions are known, and He beautified the night sky with shining lamps that invite every thoughtful observer to recognize the wisdom and power of the Creator.

phrases.translation: And We protected it from every accursed devil
phrases.explanation: God has guarded the heavens and preserved them from every rebellious, outcast devil who has been driven away from divine mercy. Because of this protection, the devils cannot enter the heavenly realms to corrupt the revelation or freely gather knowledge of the unseen decrees that God entrusts to His angels for His messengers on earth.

phrases.translation: except the one eavesdropping, who is then pursued by a visible flare
phrases.explanation: Whenever a rebellious devil attempts to sneak near the lower heaven to eavesdrop on the conversation of the angels about upcoming decrees, a bright, piercing flame of fire immediately chases him down. This shooting star strikes or drives away the eavesdropper before he can corrupt the truth, though he may sometimes toss a snatched word to a fortune-teller below before the flame overtakes him, mixing it with countless lies.

phrases.translation: As for the earth, We spread it out and placed upon it firm mountains,
phrases.explanation: After mentioning His signs in the heavens, God points to His signs on the earth, which He stretched out as a wide, habitable expanse for living creatures. Upon it He set heavy, deeply rooted mountains like pegs and anchors so that the earth remains stable and does not shake or tilt beneath its inhabitants.

phrases.translation: and caused everything to grow there in perfect balance
phrases.explanation: Out of the earth God brings forth every kind of plant, crop, and provision in a known, measured proportion suited to the needs of creation. Commentators explained that this balance means every species is produced in the exact measure decreed by God’s wisdom, neither exceeding nor falling short of what sustains life across different lands and seasons.

phrases.translation: And We made in it means of sustenance for you and others, who you do not provide for
phrases.explanation: In the earth God has provided food, clothing, farming, trade, and every way of making a living for human beings, as well as sustenance for countless dependents and creatures whom people do not truly feed. Commentators explained that these others include livestock, wild animals, birds, and even servants and family members, for although people may care for them outwardly, it is God alone Who actually provides their sustenance.

phrases.translation: There is not any means ˹of sustenance˺ whose reserves We do not hold,
phrases.explanation: Every good thing and every provision that exists in creation, especially rain and the blessings that grow from it, comes exclusively from the inexhaustible treasuries of God. Nothing lies outside His ownership and control, and no creature possesses independent storehouses of life, wealth, or mercy apart from what God holds in His hand.

phrases.translation: only bringing it forth in precise measure
phrases.explanation: God sends down rain and every form of provision from His storehouses only in a known, decreed quantity according to His wisdom and what benefits His servants. Early interpreters noted that He gives more to some regions and less to others, not out of any shortage in His treasuries, but because He apportions every blessing in the exact measure He wills.

phrases.translation: We send fertilizing winds, and bring down rain from the sky for you to drink.
phrases.explanation: God sends the winds to pollinate trees and plants and to fill the clouds with moisture, just as a pregnant bearer carries its load, until rain pours down from the sky. Through this cycle He provides fresh, sweet water for human beings, their livestock, and their crops, turning barren land into thriving gardens.

phrases.translation: It is not you who hold its reserves
phrases.explanation: Human beings are not the keepers or owners of the storehouses of rain and water, nor do they have the power to hold it back when God sends it or to bring it down when He withholds it. Because God alone controls these reserves, people should recognize their complete dependence on Him and worship Him alone with gratitude.

phrases.translation: Surely it is We Who give life and cause death.
phrases.explanation: God alone brings living beings into existence from nothing, breathes life into the dead earth and into human bodies, and decrees death when each appointed lifespan comes to an end. Since He has already demonstrated His power to originate life and end it, raising the dead on the Day of Resurrection is entirely within His power.

phrases.translation: And We are the ˹Eternal˺ Successor
phrases.explanation: When the earth and every creature upon it eventually perish, God alone remains as the ultimate Inheritor of all creation. Earthly kings, wealthy owners, and whole generations pass away and leave behind everything they claimed to possess, while everything returns to God, the Ever-Living Who never dies.

phrases.translation: We certainly know those who have gone before you and those who will come after ˹you˺
phrases.explanation: Nothing about humanity is hidden from God’s knowledge, whether the earlier generations who have already lived and died or the later generations who are still alive and yet to be born. Early commentators also mentioned another explanation, that this refers to those who step forward into the front ranks of prayer or battle and those who stand in the back rows, showing that God knows every person’s station and intention.

phrases.translation: Surely your Lord ˹alone˺ will gather them together ˹for judgment˺. He is truly All-Wise, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Judgment, your Lord will certainly assemble all human beings, from the very first generation to the very last, so that none is left behind. He is All-Wise in how He governs their lives and decrees their reckoning, and All-Knowing of every deed they performed and every particle of their scattered remains.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We created man from sounding clay moulded from black mud
phrases.explanation: God reminds humanity of its humble origin in Adam, whom He fashioned from dry, hardened clay that makes a ringing sound when struck, formed out of dark mud whose color and odor had changed over time. By recalling that human beings were shaped from lifeless earth, God exposes the folly of human arrogance and shows that human dignity comes from God’s honoring creation.

phrases.translation: As for the jinn, We created them earlier from smokeless fire
phrases.explanation: Before creating Adam from clay, God created the father of the jinn from a fierce, scorching flame of fire free of smoke. Some early interpreters described it as the pure tongue of fire or a blazing, hot wind that penetrates through the pores. This contrast between clay and fire later became the pretext for Satan’s arrogant refusal to bow.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember, O Prophet˺ when your Lord said to the angels, “I am going to create a human being from sounding clay moulded from black mud
phrases.explanation: God instructs the Prophet to remind his people of the moment when the Lord announced to the angels that He was about to create a mortal human being out of dry, ringing clay shaped from dark, altered mud. By informing the angels beforehand and giving them His command, God prepared the test that would distinguish true obedience from hidden pride.

phrases.translation: So when I have fashioned him and had a spirit of My Own ˹creation˺ breathed into him, fall down in prostration to him.”
phrases.explanation: God commanded the angels that once He had completed shaping Adam’s body in due proportion and breathed into him the spirit created by Him, so that Adam became a living, speaking human being, they must all bow down before him. This prostration was not an act of worship directed to Adam, but a greeting of honor and an act of obedience to God’s command.

phrases.translation: So the angels prostrated all together—
phrases.explanation: As soon as God breathed the spirit into Adam, every single angel obeyed their Lord’s command without hesitation or pride, bowing down together in honor of Adam. Not one of the angels held back or questioned the wisdom of God, demonstrating their complete submission and devotion to whatever their Creator ordains.

phrases.translation: but not Iblîs, who refused to prostrate with the others
phrases.explanation: Iblis alone broke away from the ranks of those who bowed and arrogantly refused to prostrate alongside the angels. Although he had been present among the angels and was addressed by the same divine command, envy and pride overtook him, leading him to disobey God openly and look down upon Adam.

phrases.translation: Allah asked, “O Iblîs! What is the matter with you that you did not join others in prostration?”
phrases.explanation: God called Iblis to account with a question of rebuke and condemnation, asking what prevented him from joining the angels who bowed down in obedience. God already knew what was in Iblis’s heart, but questioned him so that his arrogance and defiance would be exposed as a lasting warning to all creation.

phrases.translation: He replied, “It is not for me to prostrate to a human You created from sounding clay moulded from black mud.”
phrases.explanation: Instead of repenting, Iblis tried to justify his disobedience by despising Adam’s physical origin, declaring that someone like himself, created from fire, should never bow to a mortal formed from dry clay and dark mud. In his pride, he looked only at outward matter and ignored both the direct command of God and the honor God had bestowed upon Adam.

phrases.translation: Allah commanded, “Then get out of Paradise, for you are truly cursed
phrases.explanation: Because Iblis met God’s command with arrogance and defiance, God ordered him to depart from Paradise or from his lofty station in the heavens. He was declared accursed and cast out, stripped of the honor he had previously enjoyed and banished from the company of the obedient angels and the mercy of God.

phrases.translation: And surely upon you is condemnation until the Day of Judgment.”
phrases.explanation: God decreed that His curse, wrath, and banishment from mercy will remain upon Iblis continuously until the Day of Recompense, when all creatures are judged and repaid for their deeds. When that Day arrives, his condemnation does not end, but turns into the eternal punishment of the Fire prepared for him and his followers.

phrases.translation: Satan appealed, “My Lord! Then delay my end until the Day of their resurrection.”
phrases.explanation: Even after being cursed, Iblis did not seek forgiveness, but asked God to grant him a postponement of death until the Day when all humanity is raised from their graves. Early commentators noted that by asking to live until the resurrection, he hoped both to escape the taste of death and to have the entire span of human history to take revenge on Adam’s descendants.

phrases.translation: Allah said, “You will be delayed
phrases.explanation: God answered Iblis’s request by decreeing that he is indeed placed among those granted a long respite in this world. As part of God’s wisdom in testing human beings so that the obedient are distinguished from the rebellious, Iblis was allowed to remain alive and active rather than being destroyed immediately.

phrases.translation: until the appointed Day.”
phrases.explanation: God did not grant Iblis survival until the resurrection when death no longer occurs, but only until the Day of the known, appointed time. Commentators explained that this appointed Day is the first blast of the Trumpet when every living creature in the heavens and the earth dies, at which point Iblis too must taste death before being raised for punishment.

phrases.translation: Satan responded, “My Lord! For allowing me to stray
phrases.explanation: Iblis attributed his own rebellion and ruin to God’s decree of misguidance, or swore by God’s trial of him through Adam’s creation, refusing to take responsibility for his own pride. Rather than turning back in humility, he used his fall into error as a reason to declare open hostility against Adam’s offspring.

phrases.translation: I will surely tempt them on earth and mislead them all together
phrases.explanation: He vowed to beautify acts of disobedience, idol worship, and worldly desires in the eyes of human beings on earth so that sin appears pleasing and profitable to them. Through whispers, false promises, and alluring temptations, he pledged to spare no effort in leading all of Adam’s descendants away from the straight path of obedience to God.

phrases.translation: except Your chosen servants among them.”
phrases.explanation: Even Iblis had to confess that he possesses no power to misguide God’s sincere, chosen servants. Depending on the two canonical readings of the Arabic word, commentators explained these either as the servants whom God has specially selected and protected by His grace, or as the believers who have purified their obedience and devotion exclusively for God.

phrases.translation: Allah said, “This is the Way, binding on Me
phrases.explanation: God declared that this is a straight, upright path leading directly back to Him, and a binding promise that He has taken upon Himself in justice and grace. Under the primary reading, commentators explained that the path of truth returns to God and rests under His watchful care, so that He rewards and protects everyone who walks upon it in sincere devotion.

phrases.translation: you will certainly have no authority over My servants,
phrases.explanation: God affirms that Iblis has no compelling power, proof, or dominance over His faithful servants by which he could force them into disbelief or sin. Whenever Satan whispers to them, they remember God and seek refuge in Him, so his plots fail to overcome their faith.

phrases.translation: except the deviant who follow you
phrases.explanation: Satan gains influence only over those wayward people who willingly obey his whispers, prefer their own desires over God’s guidance, and choose to follow him into idolatry and rebellion. They are not overpowered against their will, but become his followers through their own deliberate choice to abandon the truth.

phrases.translation: and surely Hell is their destined place, all together
phrases.explanation: Hell is the fixed, inescapable meeting place promised for Iblis and every one of the deviant followers who obeyed him in the world. Although Satan promised them pleasure and success on earth, the final destination to which he actually leads his entire company is the punishment of the Fire.

phrases.translation: It has seven gates, to each a group of them is designated.”
phrases.explanation: Hell is structured with seven gates, which early interpreters explained as seven levels or tiers stacked one below another according to the severity of punishment. Each gate has an allotted share of Iblis’s followers assigned to enter through it and dwell in its tier, matched in full justice to the gravity of their disbelief and evil deeds.

phrases.translation: Indeed, the righteous will be amid Gardens and springs
phrases.explanation: In contrast to the followers of Satan, those who feared God by obeying His commands and avoiding idolatry and sin will dwell among lush gardens of trees and flowing springs of water. Their reverent awe of God in the world is rewarded with lasting delight and refreshment in Paradise.

phrases.translation: ˹It will be said to them,˺ “Enter in peace and security.”
phrases.explanation: As the righteous enter Paradise, the angels greet them on God’s behalf and welcome them to enter in complete peace and safety. They are forever secure from any punishment, fear, death, or sorrow, and completely safe from ever losing the blessings and honor that God has bestowed upon them.

phrases.translation: We will remove whatever bitterness they had in their hearts.
phrases.explanation: God purifies the hearts of the people of Paradise by stripping away every trace of resentment, envy, rancor, or worldly hostility that ever existed between them on earth. Commentators noted that once believers are cleansed of all malice as they enter the Garden, nothing remains in their hearts toward one another except pure affection and peace.

phrases.translation: In a friendly manner, they will be on thrones, facing one another
phrases.explanation: United as loving brothers with purified hearts, the inhabitants of Paradise recline on raised couches and thrones, facing one another in warm companionship and joyful conversation. They never turn their backs on one another, enjoying mutual honor and fellowship in the presence of their Lord.

phrases.translation: No fatigue will touch them there, nor will they ever be asked to leave
phrases.explanation: In those gardens the righteous will never experience any weariness, hardship, or exhaustion, unlike life on earth where even pleasure is followed by fatigue. Better still, their joy is never shadowed by the fear of loss, for they will never be driven out of Paradise or deprived of the eternal bliss God has granted them.

phrases.translation: Inform My servants ˹O Prophet˺ that I am truly the All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: God commands the Prophet to proclaim to His servants the glad tidings that He is the All-Forgiving and Most Merciful toward everyone who repents and turns back to Him in obedience. He conceals the sins of the repentant without disgracing them and shows them mercy by lifting punishment from them after they abandon their wrongdoing.

phrases.translation: and that My torment is indeed the most painful
phrases.explanation: Alongside the promise of mercy, the Prophet must also warn them that God’s punishment for those who persist in disbelief and rebellion without repentance is an agonizing torment unmatched by any other suffering. Pairing boundless forgiveness with severe punishment keeps believers balanced between sincere hope in God’s mercy and reverent fear of disobeying Him.

phrases.translation: And inform them ˹O Prophet˺ about Abraham’s guests
phrases.explanation: God instructs the Prophet to relate to his people the story of the honored guests who visited Abraham, the friend of the Merciful. Those guests were angels sent in human form to bring Abraham glad tidings of a son and then carry out God’s judgment against the wicked people of Lot.

phrases.translation: who entered upon him and greeted ˹him with˺, “Peace!”
phrases.explanation: When the angels came into Abraham’s presence in the form of strangers, they greeted him with the word of peace. Abraham welcomed them as guests and hurried to set a roasted calf before them, not yet realizing that his visitors were heavenly messengers who do not eat earthly food.

phrases.translation: He ˹later˺ said, “Surely we are afraid of you.”
phrases.explanation: When Abraham saw that their hands did not reach toward the meal he had prepared for them, he grew fearful and told them that he and his household were apprehensive of them. In the custom of his land, a guest who refused to eat the host’s food was suspected of having come with hostile or harmful intentions.

phrases.translation: They reassured ˹him˺, “Do not be afraid! Surely we give you good news of a knowledgeable son.”
phrases.explanation: The angels immediately calmed Abraham’s fear and revealed their true mission of grace toward his household, announcing the glad tidings that God would grant him a son endowed with deep understanding and wisdom. Commentators identified this promised son as Isaac, who would grow up to possess prophetic knowledge and devotion to God.

phrases.translation: He wondered, “Do you give me good news despite my old age?
phrases.explanation: Abraham expressed amazement at this announcement because both he and his wife Sarah had reached advanced old age, long past the ordinary years of childbearing. He did not doubt God’s almighty power, but marveled in astonishment that such a blessing was being granted to him after old age had already overtaken his body.

phrases.translation: What unlikely news!”
phrases.explanation: In wonder and joy, Abraham asked how and with what extraordinary promise they were bringing him this glad news at such a late stage of life. His question sought confirmation of whether this child was a miraculous gift directly decreed by God beyond the usual course of nature.

phrases.translation: They responded, “We give you good news in all truth, so do not be one of those who despair.”
phrases.explanation: The angels assured him that their glad tidings came with absolute certainty and true knowledge from God, Whose decree never fails. They urged him not to be like those who lose hope in God’s grace, but to receive the promise with full confidence in the mercy of his Lord.

phrases.translation: He exclaimed, “Who would despair of the mercy of their Lord except the misguided?”
phrases.explanation: Abraham declared that he was far from despairing, affirming that no one gives up hope in the mercy of his Lord except those who have strayed from the path of truth. Anyone who truly knows God’s boundless power and generosity remains confident in His mercy, showing that Abraham’s earlier question arose from joyful wonder rather than doubt.

phrases.translation: He ˹then˺ added, “What is your mission, O messenger-angels?”
phrases.explanation: Once Abraham understood that these visitors were angels sent by God and had received their glad tidings, he asked what further command or weighty errand had brought them down in this manner. He realized that a group of angels would not descend in such form unless they had been charged with a momentous decree.

phrases.translation: They replied, “We have actually been sent to a wicked people
phrases.explanation: The angels informed Abraham that God had dispatched them to destroy a criminal nation steeped in disbelief and shameless corruption, referring to the people of Lot in the cities of Sodom. Because those people persisted in defying God and committing indecency after every warning, the decree for their annihilation had arrived.

phrases.translation: As for the family of Lot, we will certainly deliver them all
phrases.explanation: Out of that doomed population, the angels announced that they would rescue the household of Lot, meaning Lot himself and his believing daughters who followed him in faith and obedience to God. None of the believers in his family would be touched by the torment descending upon the city.

phrases.translation: except his wife. We have determined that she will be one of the doomed.”
phrases.explanation: Lot’s wife was excluded from deliverance because she shared in her people’s disbelief and secretly aided them by signaling when guests arrived at Lot’s home. God had already decreed that she would remain behind among those who lingered in the city and perish in the same punishment that struck her people.

phrases.translation: So when the messengers came to the family of Lot
phrases.explanation: Departing from Abraham, the angelic messengers traveled to the city of Sodom and arrived at the house of Lot in the appearance of handsome young men. Neither Lot nor his townspeople knew at first that these travelers were angels sent by God to execute His judgment.

phrases.translation: he said, “You are surely an unfamiliar people!”
phrases.explanation: Seeing strangers of striking appearance enter his home without knowing where they came from or what they intended, Lot told them that they were unfamiliar people whom he did not recognize. He felt deeply anxious for their safety, knowing the corrupt habits of his townspeople whenever foreign visitors arrived in their city.

phrases.translation: They responded, “We have come to you with that ˹torment˺ which they have doubted
phrases.explanation: The angels revealed their true identity to comfort Lot, explaining that they were God’s messengers bringing the very punishment that his people had mocked and doubted whenever he warned them. What the disbelievers had dismissed as an empty threat was now about to descend upon them.

phrases.translation: We come to you with the truth, and we are certainly truthful
phrases.explanation: The angels assured Lot that they had come with the certain, inescapable decree of God’s punishment rather than an idle warning. They affirmed that they were completely truthful in telling him that his wicked townspeople would be destroyed at daybreak while he and his believing family would be saved.

phrases.translation: So travel with your family in the dark of night, and follow ˹closely˺ behind them.
phrases.explanation: The angels instructed Lot to set out from the city with his believing family after a portion of the night had passed, and to walk behind them at the rear of the group. By following behind his daughters, he could guard them and ensure that none of his family lagged behind in the doomed city.

phrases.translation: Do not let any of you look back, and go where you are commanded.”
phrases.explanation: They were strictly commanded that not a single one of them should turn around to look back when they heard the cry of punishment descending on their people, nor tarry along the way. Instead, they were to press forward steadily toward the land where God had commanded them to seek safety.

phrases.translation: We revealed to him this decree: “Those ˹sinners˺ will be uprooted in the morning.”
phrases.explanation: God revealed His decisive verdict to Lot that the very last remnant of those disbelievers would be cut off and utterly destroyed as morning broke. From the first of them to the last, the entire corrupt community would be uprooted at daybreak so that none of them would survive.

phrases.translation: And there came the men of the city, rejoicing
phrases.explanation: When the inhabitants of Sodom heard that handsome young strangers had arrived as guests in the house of Lot, they hurried toward his home rejoicing and congratulating one another. Their wicked joy sprang from their eagerness to commit the shameful indecency for which their city was notorious.

phrases.translation: Lot pleaded, “Indeed, these are my guests, so do not embarrass me
phrases.explanation: Before the angels revealed their identity, Lot stood before his people and appealed to their sense of duty toward hospitality, reminding them that these visitors were under his protection as guests. He begged them not to humiliate and disgrace him by harming those who had sought shelter in his home.

phrases.translation: Fear Allah and do not humiliate me.”
phrases.explanation: Lot urged his townspeople to fear God’s wrath and punishment, warning them against violating the sacred bounds of God and bringing shame upon him in front of his guests. Even in the face of an aggressive mob, he called them to remember God and abandon their foul intention.

phrases.translation: They responded, “Have we not forbidden you from protecting anyone?”
phrases.explanation: Hardened in their shamelessness, the townspeople retorted that they had already forbidden Lot from hosting or offering protection to any stranger from the outside world. Whenever travelers passed through their land, Lot tried to shelter them from abuse, and his people resented his interference with their corrupt desires.

phrases.translation: He said, “O my people! Here are my daughters ˹so marry them˺ if you wish to do so.”
phrases.explanation: Seeking to turn them away from forbidden indecency and protect his guests, Lot directed his people toward lawful marriage with the women of their community, whom a prophet addresses as his daughters, or offered marriage to his own daughters. He urged them to satisfy their desires only in the pure way God had permitted.

phrases.translation: By your life ˹O Prophet˺, they certainly wandered blindly, intoxicated ˹by lust˺
phrases.explanation: God swears an oath by the life of the Prophet Muhammad, an honor early commentators noted was never granted to any other human being, to emphasize the madness of those sinners. Whether referring to Lot’s people in their lust or to Quraysh in their heedlessness, they stumbled blindly like drunkards who cannot see right guidance.

phrases.translation: So the ˹mighty˺ blast overtook them at sunrise
phrases.explanation: Just as the sun rose on the appointed morning, the terrifying cry of divine punishment struck the people of Lot all at once. Their night of drunken arrogance ended in an instant as the deafening blast seized them at sunrise, leaving them no chance to flee or defend themselves.

phrases.translation: And We turned the cities ˹of Sodom and Gomorrah˺ upside down and rained upon them stones of baked clay
phrases.explanation: God overturned their cities so that their highest parts became their lowest, burying their homes and streets beneath them, and followed that upheaval with a rain of hard stones made of baked clay. Thus the punishment matched the perversity of a people who had inverted the natural order God created.

phrases.translation: Surely in this are signs for those who contemplate
phrases.explanation: In the utter destruction of Lot’s people and their overturned cities are unmistakable signs and lessons for those who examine things with keen insight and reflection. When thoughtful observers look upon the ruins of that land, they recognize the certain outcome awaiting everyone who denies God’s messengers and persists in rebellion.

phrases.translation: Their ruins still lie along a known route
phrases.explanation: The ruined site of Sodom lies directly along a clear, well-known highway that the caravans of Quraysh regularly pass on their journeys between Mecca and Syria. Because those desolate ruins remain fixed in plain sight along their travel route, the Meccan disbelievers cannot claim ignorance of how God punished earlier sinners.

phrases.translation: Surely in this is a sign for those who believe
phrases.explanation: What God did to the people of Lot stands as a clear proof and a reassuring sign for those who believe in God and His Messenger. It confirms for the believers that God’s promise is true, that He ultimately destroys the persistent wrongdoers, and that He rescues the people of faith when punishment descends.

phrases.translation: And the residents of the Forest were truly wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: The inhabitants of the Wood, who lived in a region of dense, intertwined trees and thickets and to whom the prophet Shuayb was sent, were likewise guilty of disbelief and injustice. Despite the lush gardens and abundant provision God granted them, they rejected their messenger and persisted in idolatry and corrupt dealings.

phrases.translation: so We inflicted punishment upon them. The ruins of both nations still lie on a well-known road
phrases.explanation: God took vengeance upon the people of the Wood by sending down a scorching heat followed by a cloud of blazing fire that consumed them. Both ruined lands, the cities of Lot and the dwellings of the people of the Wood, lie along an open, unmistakable road by which travelers guide their journeys and witness the fate of the disobedient.

phrases.translation: Indeed, the residents of the Stone Valley also denied the messengers
phrases.explanation: The inhabitants of the Stone Valley of al-Hijr, the tribe of Thamud who lived in the rocky valley between Hijaz and Syria, likewise rejected the truth. Although they directly denied their prophet Salih, denying one messenger of God is counted as denying all the messengers because they all bring the same call to worship God alone.

phrases.translation: We gave them Our signs, but they turned away from them
phrases.explanation: God showed the people of Thamud clear proofs and miraculous signs confirming the truth of Salih’s message, including the she-camel brought forth as a sign from God. Yet instead of taking warning and believing, they stubbornly turned their backs on those proofs, refused to reflect upon them, and hamstrung the she-camel in defiance.

phrases.translation: They carved their homes in the mountains, feeling secure
phrases.explanation: With great skill and strength, the people of Thamud hewed sturdy dwellings directly into the solid rock of the mountains. Commentators explained that they felt completely safe from God’s punishment, or secure that their stone-carved homes would never collapse or be breached, imagining that rock walls could shield them from death and judgment.

phrases.translation: But the ˹mighty˺ blast overtook them in the morning
phrases.explanation: After they slaughtered the she-camel and were warned that they had only three more days to enjoy their homes, the terrifying cry of destruction seized them as morning broke on the fourth day. Their mountain fortresses could not keep out the blast of God’s decree when their appointed hour arrived.

phrases.translation: and all they achieved was of no help to them
phrases.explanation: Neither the wealth and power that the people of Thamud had amassed nor the fortified houses they had carved into the rocky mountains availed them in the least when God’s punishment descended. All their worldly achievements and wicked schemes proved utterly powerless to ward off the decree of God.

phrases.translation: We have not created the heavens and the earth and everything in between except for a purpose.
phrases.explanation: God did not create the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them in vain or out of injustice, but only in truth, wisdom, and equity. Just as He destroyed those rebellious nations with complete justice because they earned their ruin, the entire universe operates by His rightful order rather than chance.

phrases.translation: And the Hour is certain to come, so forgive graciously
phrases.explanation: Because the Hour of Resurrection is certain and will surely arrive to settle every account between the Prophet and his opponents, God instructs him to bear their insults patiently and overlook their harm with a gracious pardon. Several early commentators noted that this command to pardon applied before permission for armed defense was later revealed.

phrases.translation: Surely your Lord is the Master Creator, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: Your Lord is the Supreme Creator Who continually brings all things into existence in wisdom and perfection, and He is All-Knowing of everything His creatures do. Because He created both you and your opponents and knows every secret of their hearts and deeds, you can entrust their affair entirely to His judgment.

phrases.translation: We have certainly granted you the seven often-repeated verses and the great Quran
phrases.explanation: God reminds the Prophet of the immense favor already bestowed upon him in revelation. Early interpreters differed over the seven often-repeated verses: many identified them as the opening chapter of the Quran, whose seven verses are repeated in every prayer, while others explained them as the seven long chapters of the Quran, joined here with the rest of the mighty Scripture.

phrases.translation: Do not let your eyes crave the ˹fleeting˺ pleasures We have provided for some of the disbelievers,
phrases.explanation: Having received the priceless treasure of the Quran, the Prophet is instructed never to cast longing eyes toward the temporary luxuries, wealth, and worldly status that God has allowed various classes of rich disbelievers to enjoy for a brief time. Compared to the eternal gift of revelation, all the ornaments of this world are small and fleeting.

phrases.translation: nor grieve for them.
phrases.explanation: God also tells the Prophet not to feel sorrow over the disbelievers’ stubborn refusal to accept faith or over the temporary prosperity they have been given before their reckoning. Their rejection harms only themselves, and their brief worldly enjoyment is followed by a severe punishment in the hereafter.

phrases.translation: And be gracious to the believers
phrases.explanation: In contrast to the arrogant wealthy elites, the Prophet is commanded to lower his wing of humility, gentleness, and compassion toward the believers who follow him. He is to draw them close, treat them with warmth and kindness, and never be harsh toward those who have embraced faith.

phrases.translation: And say, “I am truly sent with a clear warning”—
phrases.explanation: God commands the Prophet to declare openly to the polytheists of Quraysh that he is a plain warner whose message leaves no ambiguity. He warns them clearly that a painful punishment from God will descend upon them if they persist in their idolatry and denial, just as it struck earlier nations.

phrases.translation: ˹a warning˺ similar to what We sent to those who divided ˹the Scriptures˺
phrases.explanation: The warning to Quraysh recalls the punishment or scripture God sent down upon the dividers and conspirators before them. Commentators differed over their identity: many said they were the People of the Book who divided their scripture by believing in some parts and rejecting others, while others said they were a band of Meccan polytheists or earlier plotters who conspired against God’s messengers.

phrases.translation: who ˹now˺ accept parts of the Quran, rejecting others
phrases.explanation: They tore the revealed Scripture into scattered pieces like the severed limbs of a slaughtered animal. According to one group of early interpreters, this describes the People of the Book who accepted parts of revelation and rejected others. According to another group, it describes the polytheists of Quraysh who split up the Quran into contradictory labels, calling it sorcery, poetry, soothsaying, or ancient fables.

phrases.translation: So by your Lord! We will certainly question them all
phrases.explanation: God swears an emphatic oath by the Lord of the Prophet that He will surely call every one of them to account on the Day of Resurrection. None who fragmented the revelation, mocked the truth, or lived on earth will escape standing before God for questioning.

phrases.translation: about what they used to do
phrases.explanation: On that Day they will be questioned about all the deeds they committed in the world and how they responded to God’s messengers and commands. Many early commentators explained that the foremost matter about which everyone will be asked is the testimony that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah, along with why they acted in disobedience.

phrases.translation: So proclaim what you have been commanded,
phrases.explanation: God commands the Prophet to declare the message openly, boldly, and publicly, cleaving through falsehood with the truth of the Quran and reciting it aloud in prayer. Early reports note that the Prophet and his companions had worshipped quietly until this verse was revealed, whereupon he came out and proclaimed Islam publicly to Quraysh.

phrases.translation: and turn away from the polytheists
phrases.explanation: As he proclaims God’s command openly, the Prophet is instructed to pay no heed to the insults, threats, and rage of the idolaters. Commentators noted that this command to turn away patiently guided the believers in Mecca before permission for armed defense was later revealed.

phrases.translation: Surely We will be sufficient for you against the mockers
phrases.explanation: God reassures the Prophet that He Himself will protect him and suffice him against the arrogant ringleaders of Quraysh who mocked him and ridiculed the Quran. Therefore he need not fear their hostility while proclaiming the message, for God’s protection shields him and brings ruin upon those who scoff at His Messenger.

phrases.translation: who set up ˹other˺ gods with Allah. They will soon come to know
phrases.explanation: Those mockers are the very ones who associate false gods and idols with God in worship while scoffing at His Messenger. God concludes with a stern threat that they will soon come to know the terrible consequences of their idolatry and mockery when punishment overtakes them in this world and on the Day of Judgment.

phrases.translation: We certainly know that your heart is truly distressed by what they say
phrases.explanation: God consoles the Prophet by assuring him that He knows full well how deeply his chest tightens with grief, sorrow, and distress when his own people accuse him of falsehood, mock the revelation, and stubbornly turn away from the guidance he brings for their salvation.

phrases.translation: So glorify the praises of your Lord and be one of those who ˹always˺ pray
phrases.explanation: Whenever the insults and rejection of the disbelievers weigh heavily on his heart, the Prophet is instructed to seek relief by glorifying God with praise, giving thanks to Him, and turning to prayer and prostration. Through constant remembrance and devotion to God, distress is lifted from the heart and replaced with strength and peace.

phrases.translation: and worship your Lord until the inevitable comes your way
phrases.explanation: God commands the Prophet to persevere steadfastly in worshipping and obeying his Lord throughout his entire life until that which is certain arrives. Early commentators agreed that the inevitable certainty mentioned here means death, teaching that a believer’s duty to worship God never ends as long as life remains.
